user_request: Do A1, A2 and B1, B2 and B3
method: Elenchus tiers A/L/C/X; claims ledger and gate per paper; positive + negative controls; producer != verifier (independent audit on Opus, never cheaper than the producer); publish per paper only after the audit (not REJECT), revision applied, Lean controls caught, and a result remains (negative results count).

items.title: Toward a complete Lean proof of the Sandier-Serfaty conjecture: port the finite certificate into Lean (A1a), begin the analytic reduction (A1b)
statements: A1a: the finite certificate's stages (record: 22 printed integer pairs + mesh stages) become kernel-checked inequalities via LeanFlow lean.* and interval arithmetic, with planted false stages rejected; report how many stages are kernel-checked and the cost of the rest.
A1b: formalize at least one complete lemma of the reduction (manuscript Sections 2-5) on top of SandierSerfatyStatement.lean and the P3 CM library; report what remains.
items.kill: no claim that the conjecture is formally proved unless every stage AND the reduction are kernel-checked

items.title: Independent rebuild, axiom audit and soundness-escape scan of the openai/NavierStokesAndEuler breakdown theorems; second fidelity audit
statements: A2a: the corpus (HEAD f9e8bc5) rebuilds from source on our machine (copy on /home), and #print axioms of navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 and navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic is within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}.

A2b: no soundness escape in the dependency closure: native_decide, implemented_by, extern, unsafe, csimp, opaque-with-unsound-impl, custom elab/macro forging output, #exit, environment manipulation, axioms; planted escapes in a scratch copy are detected (negative controls).
A2c: a second, independent statement-fidelity audit vs Fefferman's official text agrees with H9 or names a mismatch.
items.kill: wording strictly 'independently rebuilt and audited'; never 'Clay problem solved'; any escape or mismatch is reported first

items.title: Quantum structural phase transition triangular -> rhombic in soft-core (Gaussian-core) crystals: critical quantum parameter hbar*(a) vs melting, beyond harmonic
statements: B1a (Tier X): E(tau) = E_static + hbar_eff E_zp loses triangular local minimality at hbar*(a) for a in (0.377,1.581); compute hbar*(a).
B1b: compare hbar* with a Lindemann melting estimate (harmonic <u^2>) at the same parameters.
B1c: anharmonic check (self-consistent harmonic approximation; path-integral Monte Carlo at a few points if feasible).
B1d (Tier L): relevance to Rydberg-dressed atoms (soft-core interactions) from verified literature.
items.kill: if the transition lies beyond melting or disappears beyond harmonic, report that (negative result)

items.title: Kernel-checked theorem: the triangular lattice is not a local minimum of the harmonic zero-point energy for the Gaussian exp(-pi r^2) (a = 1)
statements: B2: the isotropic curvature Lap E_zp at the triangular point is negative for a = 1, certified by interval arithmetic with rigorous tail bounds and checked in Lean (LeanFlow data certificate + ProgZeroPoint lemmas); negative control: a = 2 (positive curvature) is not certified negative.
items.kill: if the rigorous enclosure cannot exclude 0, report the best certified interval

items.title: Feasibility study: can the Sandier-Serfaty Voronoi-comparison + certificate architecture reach 3D Coulomb jellium (bcc) crystallization?
statements: B3: a step-by-step analysis of which steps of the 2D proof are dimension-specific, whether a 3D Voronoi comparison bound exists, an estimate of 3D certificate size, and a credible attack plan or a reasoned negative assessment; literature: bcc among lattices (arXiv 2610.29732) and the 3D crystallization literature.
